column15: Peat RESTORED to light this session: springbank.scot's own "Whisky" range page (opened via browser, past the earlier 403) states Springbank itself uses "lightly peated barley" -- producer-domain corroboration per this round's rule. The same page independently confirms sibling Longrow is "heavily peated" and Hazelburn is "air dried only" (unpeated, not in this batch), matching the sibling-brand split. Re-opened both inherited citations this session too: Wikipedia and scotchwhisky.com's Whiskypedia (both re-fetched) each independently characterize Springbank as "medium-peated" at 8-10ppm malt spec, versus Longrow's 50ppm/48-hour smoke and Hazelburn's 0ppm -- a genuine light/medium boundary disagreement between the distillery's own marketing word ("lightly peated") and third-party ppm-based grading, exactly as the prior round flagged. Kept light per the producer's own domain wording, which is what this round's rule privileges, but a human should feel free to override to medium given the ppm figures above. Kind/country/region/owner/type unchanged (Wikipedia, scotchwhisky.com Whiskypedia, both confirming Campbeltown / J&A Mitchell & Company).

Upgraded from low to high this session: blockgreyandblock.com (opened via browser, past the earlier 403/406 -- the merchant is still trading, est. 1786, Park Lane/Mayfair) states in its own words "The Speaker Blended Scotch Whisky ... first crafted for one of our customers: The Speaker of the House of Commons," and describes the whisky as "a light coloured, soft whisky with elegant overtones of fruitiness and with pleasant hints of vanilla and pear drops" -- no smoke/peat mentioned anywhere, so peat=none now rests on the producer's own domain rather than category default alone. whiskyauctioneer.com (opened via browser) independently confirms a real 43%/75cl bottling under this name.

Peat RESTORED to medium this session: got past nikka.com's age gate via browser (country United States, DOB) and reached the brand's own page, which states "Yoichi malts are described as bold and strong with refined peaty notes and smokiness brought by the traditional direct coal-fired distillation," and separately frames a 2021 "Non-Peated" limited edition as a deliberate departure "from the preconceived 'peaty' image of Yoichi" -- confirming the standard range is peated, on Nikka's own domain. Kept at medium rather than heavy per the retry goal's framing (house style, not Islay-extreme); no on-domain ppm figure was found to sharpen this further. Re-opened Wikipedia this session too, confirming Hokkaido location, 1934 founding and Nikka Whisky Distilling ownership (the article itself is silent on peat/flavour). Kind/country/owner/type unchanged.

Fully verified this session (never searched before -- quota). Big Moustache is a Tennessee whiskey + American single malt brand from BBC Spirits (Bogdan and Bertrand Company, Bordeaux, France; founded 2010 by Bogdan Tanasoiu and Bertrand Fradin), distilled/bottled in the US -- flaviar.com states "made and bottled in Tennessee" via the Lincoln County maple-charcoal process, and sklep-domwhisky.pl names the actual distiller as "Tennessee Distilling Co." Corrected kind from blend to brand (Tennessee whiskey and single malt are not blends) and countryCode from the catalogue's inconsistent DE/US majority-vote to a confirmed US (production origin); BBC Spirits is a French marketer of an American-made spirit. defaultTypeName left empty: the portfolio spans Tennessee whiskey and American single malt. peatProfile=none: sources describe "slightly smoky"/"a distant trace of smoke" tasting notes explicitly attributed to the maple-charcoal mellowing (Lincoln County Process), not peated malt -- no peat mentioned anywhere.

Found the current live domain this session (cedarridgedistillery.com loads cleanly via browser -- no 403/parking). Iowa's first distillery, 1441 Marak Rd, Swisher, Iowa. Confirms an Iowa Straight Bourbon / rye / American single malt range, so defaultTypeName stays empty (matches the catalogue's own Bourbon + Wheat samples). peatProfile=none for the mainline (Iowa Straight Bourbon, Wheat whiskey -- corn/wheat/rye mash bills, never peated malt), but flagging for a human: the distillery's own "Special Release"/"Single Cask Series" American-single-malt page lists a one-off "Peated Malt in Amontillado Sherry" release -- not represented by any of this row's catalogue sample names (Cedar Ridge / Cedar Ridge Iowa / Cedar Ridge Wheat), so left out of scope rather than added as a rule.

Current owner resolved this session: Stock Spirits Group completed its purchase of Clan Campbell Limited from Pernod Ricard/Chivas Brothers on 5 September 2023 (beveragedaily.com, opened) -- a leading blend-12yo Scotch brand in France, also sold in Spain/Luxembourg/Italy. Re-opened the two inherited citations this session too: Wikipedia's Scotch whisky article does not mention Clan Campbell but confirms blended Scotch is ~90% of Scottish production aiming for a consistent house style, and thewhiskeywash.com's peat-levels guide (also re-opened) likewise does not mention Clan Campbell but confirms Speyside/Lowland houses are typically unpeated. Kind/country/peat unchanged (ordinary blended Scotch, no smoke evidence).

Current owner resolved this session: Halewood Artisanal Spirits still owns the Crabbie whisky brand and its own Bonnington Distillery in Leith as of August 2025 (sltn.co.uk, opened -- distillery manager Gregor Butchert quoted). A same-month sale (just-drinks.com, opened) moved only the "Crabbie's" alcoholic-ginger-beer/ginger-wine brand and IP to Brookfield Drinks -- explicitly "no production assets" and no mention of whisky/Bonnington -- so the two businesses sharing the Crabbie name now have different owners; this row is the whisky line only. "Crabbie and Cree"/"Crabbie&Cree" sample remains unresolved. Re-opened both inherited Wikipedia pages this session too: the Crabbie's article confirms the 1980s Macdonald & Muir/Glenmorangie chain and a 2007 sale to Halewood; the Halewood International article confirms the ginger-wine brand was bought in 2002 and, separately, that the corporate name itself changed from "Halewood International" to "Halewood Artisanal Spirits" in April 2021 -- explaining why the current legal name differs from the seed's. peat=none per ordinary-blend convention (unchanged; no smoke evidence found).

Upgraded from low to high this session: got past the 403 via browser (eganswhiskey.com is real and live; the WAF is inconsistent -- some paths 403'd again on retry). Its own "Our Story" page states "In 1852 Patrick Egan Sr. and his brother Henry established P. & H. Egan Ltd. in Tullamore," confirming the general-knowledge owner the seed/prior round could not cite. Range (Vintage Grain, Fortitude, Legacy Reserve Series III) still spans styles, so defaultTypeName stays empty. Re-opened the Irish whiskey Wikipedia article this session too: confirms peat is "rarely used in the malting process outside of Scotland," naming Cooley, Pearse Lyons and Echlinville as the known peated exceptions -- Egan's is not among them. peat=none kept per that verified convention; no producer-domain peat statement found for this brand specifically.

Peat RESTORED to light this session: got past house.suntory.com's date-of-birth gate via browser and reached the brand's own page, which states "Hakushu Whisky is the delicious and gently smoky single malt whisky with herbal notes" -- producer-domain corroboration of a light/gentle smoke house style, distinct from the same site's mention of specific heavier "peat and peated malts" special (2024 Tsukuriwake Selection) expressions. Re-opened Wikipedia this session too: confirms Yamanashi/Suntory/1973, silent on the core range's peat but corroborates that a 2013 "Heavily Peated 48%" bottling was a limited exception, not the standard style. Kind/country/owner/type unchanged.

column7: Marussia Beverages BV / Haydn Holding AB
column15: Ownership conflict RESOLVED this session -- it turns out not to be a real conflict: in a direct interview (nomunication.jp, opened), founder Kimio Yonezawa states "The Akashi Sake Brewery, Torabhaig Distillery and Mossburn Distillers are all part of a family-owned Swedish investment company" (Marussia Beverages BV / Haydn Holding AB per company-registry search results), while he personally remains the hands-on "owner-Toji" (4th-generation master brewer/distiller) running Kaikyo Distillery day to day. So "Mossburn" and "Yonezawa/Akashi" are both correct at different levels (holding company vs. operator). kaikyodistillery.com is a parked domain, not the real site (opened via browser, confirmed a Japanese registrar's parking page); akashisakebrewery.com returned 503 on every attempt (genuinely down, not just blocked). The official brand site hatozakiwhisky.com/pages/about (opened) names Yonezawa as founder but states no corporate ownership. peatProfile kept unknown: Yonezawa's own quote calls Hatozaki's finish "a light touch of smoke and honey," real evidence but from trade press (nomunication.jp), not the producer's own domain, so per this round's rule it is withheld. withheld peat proposal: light, per the Yonezawa interview above. defaultTypeName empty: range spans Finest Blended, Pure Malt and Triple Cask Reserve.

Fully verified this session (quota-starved before). whiskysaga.com (opened) states "This is a product bottled in Belgium by Sodiko NV" -- Kentucky Straight Bourbon, NAS, 40% ABV, distilled in Kentucky/USA but sourced by the Belgian bottler rather than named to a specific distillery ("no information on who the source might be"). sodiko.be (opened) confirms Sodiko is a real Belgian beverage bottler (Diepenbeek, Flanders) offering private-label/co-pack spirits, though it does not name Kentucky Jack specifically on its own site. Corrected kind from blend to brand (Straight Bourbon is not a blend) and set defaultTypeName=bourbon. peat=none per bourbon mash-bill convention; no evidence otherwise.

Fully verified this session (quota-starved before). Got past the age gate via browser; beveland.com's own product page states "Imported from Canada, Kindilan is a well-known blended whisky, mellow and aromatic, full-bodied and smooth," 70cl/1L, 40% ABV. Beveland Distillers markets/imports it (the actual Canadian distillery of origin is not named on this page). Confirms countryCode=CA independently of the catalogue's own "Канадіан" naming, and confirms kind=blend and defaultTypeName=blend. peat=none per Canadian blended whisky convention; no smoke/peat mentioned.

Peat RESTORED to heavy this session: got past laggwhisky.com's age gate via browser (it accepted a click-through this time). Its own "Our Whiskies" page states outright "At Lagg we create a heavily peated, modern and characterful single malt scotch whisky" -- direct producer-domain corroboration. The "Our Approach" page adds detail: barley "dried in a kiln of burning peat," giving "rich, smoky flavour," explicitly contrasted with "the unpeated range produced at the Lochranza Distillery" (sister site, Arran). Re-opened Wikipedia this session too: confirms 2019 opening, Isle of Arran Distillers Ltd ownership, island single malt classification, and "heavily peated malted barley (~50 ppm phenols)" -- fully consistent with the producer-domain wording. Kind/country/owner/region/type unchanged.

Peat RESTORED to heavy this session: springbank.scot's own "Whisky" range page (opened via browser) states "Today, our heavily peated, wonderfully smoky whisky is available in three bottlings" for Longrow -- producer-domain corroboration per this round's rule, from the same page that also independently confirms sibling Springbank as "lightly peated." Re-opened Wikipedia this session too: confirms Longrow at a 50ppm malt spec / 48-hour peat smoke, clearly heavy on any reading, and reconfirms J&A Mitchell & Company / Campbeltown. Kind/country/region/owner/type/parentSlug unchanged.

Fully verified this session (quota-starved before). scotchwhisky.com's Whiskypedia (opened) confirms the believed Wemyss Malts link directly: "Wemyss Malts produces Lord Elcho, a Fife-based blender and bottler established in 2005 by William Wemyss," continuing to own the brand from 2012; a blended Scotch (not blended malt) with a NAS and 15yo expression, both 40%. Set bottlerSlug=wemyss-malts (live). Tasting notes are "fruity, grassy and sweet" (NAS) / "spicier" (15yo) -- no smoke, supporting peat=none over the seed's unknown.

Fully verified this session (quota-starved before; the seed and prior round found only an unrelated legendary-king Wikipedia hit). "Maen" ("perfect circle" in Japanese) is a real Japanese whisky blend imported to the US by Shaw-Ross International Importers (shawross.com, opened): 20% malt / 80% grain whisky, double-copper-pot distilled, aged 3-5 years in ex-bourbon barrels. The actual Japanese producing distillery is not named on this page. Three expressions (blend, 8yo blended pure malt, 12yo blended pure malt) span sub-types, so defaultTypeName is left empty. peat=none: flavour profile is apple/peach/nuts/spice/honey with no smoke mentioned.

Fully verified this session (quota-starved before), confirmed exactly per the retry goal. Meikle Toir is The GlenAllachie Distillery's peated single malt brand (meikletoir.com, opened: "Guided by Master Distiller Billy Walker ... The GlenAllachie Distillery ... Speyside, Scotland ... our peated single malt serves up a sweet smoke style"). theglenallachie.com's own news article (opened) states the core range's spirit is peated to "35 PPM" using mainland (St Fergus) peat for "a more sweet and oaky smoke style" versus coastal peat, with a "Turbo" expression at 71 PPM. The three catalogue sample names (The Chinquapin, The Original, The Sherry) exactly match three of the four core-range names the article lists (Original One, Chinquapin One, Sherry One, Turbo) -- confirms this row's identity precisely. Set parentSlug=glenallachie (live). Corrected countryCode from XX to GB-SCT and region/legalRegion to speyside now that the distillery is identified; the seed's "Chinquapin" cask-type ambiguity is resolved -- Chinquapin oak is simply one of GlenAllachie's own cask choices, not evidence of American origin.

Resolved this session per the retry goal -- it is Phenomenal Spirits, not Rare Character (a different, similarly-sourced brand that surfaced in the same searches). ry3whiskey.com (opened) confirms "AMERICAN RYE WHISKEY EST. 2020," "a special blend of 3 phenomenal whiskeys, 3 carefully handpicked mash-bills, and 3 distinctive aged statements," with cask finishes (rum, madeira, toasted barrel, tokaji) matching the catalogue's own sample names. phenomenalspirits.com (opened) cross-links to ry3whiskey.com and lists RY3 Rum Cask Finish in its own portfolio, confirming the bottler. Neither site names the actual source distillery/state (a sourced/blended rye brand). Set countryCode=US and defaultTypeName=rye. peat=none: no smoke/peat mentioned; American rye mash bill.

Fully verified this session -- got past the earlier DNS/certificate failure (adrattray.com now loads cleanly via browser). A.D. Rattray's own page confirms: Stronachie distillery (built 1890s by Alexander & MacDonald in the Ochil Mountains, Perthshire; A.D. Rattray "proudly distributed the brand" historically; closed 1928) was recreated by A.D. Rattray using spirit from Benrinnes Distillery, matured in ex-bourbon casks, bottled as "Stronachie 10 Year Old Single Malt Scotch Whisky" at 43%. Corrected kind from blend to brand (this is explicitly single malt, not a blend) and defaultTypeName to single malt. Set region/legalRegion=highland per the site's own "Highland Single Malt" framing (the brand's historic Perthshire identity; the sourcing spirit itself is from Speyside's Benrinnes, but the bottling is marketed and identified as Highland). Tasting notes ("soft honey, earthy heather, malty sweetness ... biscuits ... pepper") mention no smoke, so peat=none replaces the seed's unknown.

Producer identified this session (never verified before). Multiple retail sources attribute The Charles House Blended Scotch Whisky (40%, 3-year, "created entirely in accordance with the Scotch Whisky Act 1988") to QSI (Quality Spirits International), "the World's No.1 Private Label Scotch Whisky supplier" and a subsidiary of William Grant & Sons -- qualityspiritsinternational.com (opened) confirms the company itself and its private-label business model and links to William Grant's own modern-slavery statement in its footer (corroborating the WGS affiliation), though it does not name "Charles House" specifically (expected -- private-label brands are typically not showcased on the manufacturer's own site). Set countryCode=GB-SCT and owner=QSI. peatProfile kept unknown rather than asserted: a personal blog review (westmeathwhiskeyworld, opened) mentions "a bit of peat influence" and "lovely smoky flavours," real but not producer-domain evidence, so it is withheld rather than promoted. withheld peat proposal: light-to-medium, per that one blogger's tasting note only.

Fully verified this session (quota-starved before). The retail listing (maudau.com.ua, opened) names the product "Віскі Wise Salmon Irish Whiskey" -- confirms countryCode=IE (a second Ukrainian retailer, Auchan, uses the identical "Wise Salmon Irish Whiskey" name per search results but 403'd on direct fetch). No producer/distillery is named (an own-label style product, matching this batch's other quota-starved rows). peatProfile kept unknown rather than none: one customer review on the opened page mentions "light notes of peat" in the aftertaste alongside caramel-honey/vanilla notes -- weak, non-producer evidence that contradicts the ordinary Irish-whiskey default, so left unresolved rather than guessed either way. withheld peat proposal: light, per that one customer review only.

Fully verified this session (quota-starved before). 15stars.com (opened) states its bourbon is "Blended and Bottled in Bardstown, Kentucky USA" -- confirms countryCode=US. "15 Stars" honors Kentucky as America's 15th state; "First West" is a sub-line name (Explorer/Small Batch/Extra Aged/Toasted Oak), not a separate producer -- both the "15 Stars Platinum" and "15 Stars First West" catalogue samples are bourbon. Corrected kind from blend to brand (bourbon is not a blend) and set defaultTypeName=bourbon. Trade press (not independently opened this session) additionally names founders Rick & Ricky Johnson and contract distillation at Bardstown Bourbon Co. peat=none: no smoke/peat mentioned; bourbon mash bill.

Fully verified this session, resolving the seed's unconfirmed Italian guess. bottegaspa.com (opened) confirms Alexander Single Malt is distilled by the Bottega family itself (Bibano di Godega di Sant'Urbano, Treviso, Italy) -- Sandro Bottega learned distilling in Brazil in 1985 and built his own whisky; double-distilled, matured a minimum of 4 years in oak, then finished at least 2 more years in barrels that previously held the family's own Chianti/Montalcino(Brunello)/Valpolicella(Amarone) wines. Three cask-finish variants (red wine, Brunello, Amarone) are all single malt, matching the catalogue's "Amarone Cask Finish" sample. Corrected countryCode from XX to IT, kind from blend to brand (this is single malt, self-distilled by Bottega, not a blend), and set defaultTypeName=single malt and owner=Bottega Spa. peat=none: no smoke/peat mentioned across the whole range description.

Fully verified this session (quota-starved before). Two independently-opened retail listings agree: novus.zakaz.ua (opened) names it "Blended Scotch whiskey" from "Great Britain," bottled by Sodiko NV (the same Belgian private-label bottler behind this batch's Kentucky Jack); balticwhiskyshop.com (opened) confirms Scotland and a "Light & Floral" honey/vanilla/buttery-biscuit profile with no smoke, crediting "Artisan Spirits Box" as producer (likely the brand-owner/trademark holder commissioning Sodiko as contract bottler -- both names may be correct at different levels, flagging for a human). One retailer (caskcartel.com, opened) contradicts itself, labeling "Origin: Scotland" in its own spec field while pasting templated prose about "Walsh Whiskey Distillery ... Ireland" and "faint smoke notes" -- treated as a templated copy-paste error, not evidence, since it conflicts with its own spec field and with two other independent sources. Confirms countryCode=GB-SCT, owner=Sodiko NV, peat=none.

Got past the 403 this session via browser (clicked through the age-verification modal; copperrivetdistillery.com is otherwise a normal, live site). Confirmed the current 4-product range directly: Masthouse Single Malt (Signature), Masthouse Single Malt (Reserve), Masthouse Grain Whisky and the limited Masthouse Guardian -- spans single malt AND single grain, so defaultTypeName stays empty, matching the seed's reasoning (and matching batch 19's independent "copper-rivet" producer row, which reached the same peat conclusion from the same product page). peatProfile set to none rather than left unknown: three full flavour-note product pages (Signature: vanilla/toffee apple/cream/pear/pepper; Grain: nutty/creamy/spiced/vanillin; Guardian: fruit/cinnamon/cream/peppercorn) and the "the-distillery" process page describe zero smoke or peat anywhere across the whole current range -- no page states "unpeated" in so many words, so this is inferred from a comprehensive absence on the producer's own domain rather than a direct quote; flagging that distinction for a human. bottlerSlug=copper-rivet references batch 19's row (not yet live, but consistent with it). Re-opened the Wikipedia England-distilleries list this session too: confirms Copper Rivet was established August 2016 in Chatham, Kent by Bob Russell and sons, and that "the first whisky release, branded Masthouse, was launched in November 2020" -- Bob Russell also matches the "our incredible founder, Bob" name in the Guardian product page.
